MATHS WORKSHEETS

Maths worksheets — printables for age 4.

Counting, numbers and number writing — printable maths practice built from our own artwork. Every sheet twins with a real game in Counting & Number Recognition (Class 24) — download the PDF, print from the page, or play online.

Counting Balloons Age 4Class 24Maths A party of balloons: count each row, then count them all. Cupcake Bakery Age 4Class 24Maths Count the cupcakes, then share them onto the baker two plates. Dinosaur Egg Rescue Age 4Class 24Maths Number the five eggs in the nest, then draw five more for the rescue. Farm Animal Lineup Age 4Class 24Maths Five friends are queueing for the barn: number them first to fifth. Garden Number Path Age 4Class 24Maths Ten stepping stones wind through the garden — number them 1 to 10. Giraffe Height Challenge Age 4Class 24Maths Four giraffes, four heights: number them 1 to 4 from shortest to tallest. Ice Cream Number Shop Age 4Class 24Maths Count the scoops, then build the cones: 1 scoop, 2 scoops, 3 scoops. Class 24 is growing: 17 of the planned 30 maths worksheets are ready now — the ones whose artwork has been uploaded. The remaining adventures appear here with their own real pages the moment their artwork lands; nothing is published before it can be printed honestly.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 24 · AGES 4 YEARS

Counting Caterpillar Worksheet for Age 4

Count every circle of the caterpillar, trace the number you find, and count rows of apples along the way.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

The caterpillar is made of ten numbered circle segments — counting them one by one, with a finger on each circle, is classic one-to-one counting practice. Tracing the numeral 10 afterwards connects “how many” with “what it looks like written down”.

  • Counting objects one by one to 10
  • Touch-counting without skipping
  • Tracing and writing the number 10
  • Counting small groups of apples

On the sheet: Count the caterpillar’s circles, trace the number, and count each apple row.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 24 · AGES 4 YEARS

Counting Apples Worksheet for Age 4

Count the apples in every row, draw exactly the right number into each basket, and trace your numbers.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Counting rows of apples practices the count-then-write sequence: how many, and what does that number look like? The basket task flips it around — now your child must DRAW a given number, which checks understanding from the other direction.

  • Counting groups of 2 to 5 apples
  • Writing numerals in answer boxes
  • Drawing a given number of objects
  • Tracing numerals 3, 5 and 10

On the sheet: Count each row, fill the baskets with the right number of apples, trace the numbers.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 24 · AGES 4 YEARS

Apple Counting Game Worksheet for Age 4

Count the apples row by row, write how many, then draw the whole basketful.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Two rows of five apples give counting-to-ten a clear shape: five here, five there, ten all together. Writing the number after counting connects how many with what it looks like, and drawing apples into the basket checks the count from the other direction — your child must produce exactly the number they just said.

  • Counting objects one by one to 10
  • Seeing 5 and 5 as two parts of 10
  • Writing the numeral 10
  • Drawing a given number of objects

On the sheet: Count each row, write the total, and draw the apples in the basket.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 24 · AGES 4 YEARS

Balloon Number Writing Worksheet for Age 4

Ten balloons, ten numbers: write 1 to 10, one balloon at a time.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Writing numbers in order is sequencing practice — every numeral has its place. The empty balloon centres give each number a big, friendly home, and saying the number out loud while writing it ties the name, the shape and the order together. One balloon per number also gives a natural stopping point: ten small wins instead of one long line.

  • Writing numerals 1 to 10 in order
  • Saying number names while writing
  • Left-to-right, top-to-bottom order
  • Careful pencil control inside a shape

On the sheet: Write 1 to 10 in the balloons, then trace the 10.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 24 · AGES 4 YEARS

Busy Bee Honey Factory Worksheet for Age 4

Count the honey drops, then fill the three jars for the busy bees.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Counting the drops row by row practices one-to-one counting, and the jars turn the total into parts: four, three and three. Sharing a set into jars is an early taste of part-whole thinking — the same idea that later becomes 4+3+3=10 — but here it stays hands-on: draw the drops, count the jar, say the number.

  • Counting groups of 4 and 6
  • Sharing a set into three groups
  • Drawing a given number of drops
  • Writing numerals to 10

On the sheet: Count the drops in each row, then draw 4, 3 and 3 drops into the jars.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 24 · AGES 4 YEARS

Butterfly Pattern Magic Worksheet for Age 4

One wing is dressed, the other is waiting: color the right wing to match the left.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Matching a colored shape to its empty twin is visual discrimination — the eyes must hold the color AND the shape in mind while finding its partner. It is also a first symmetry lesson: butterfly wings are the friendliest mirror there is. Finishing the wing gives a satisfying pattern moment without a single wrong answer.

  • Matching colors shape by shape
  • Noticing mirror symmetry
  • Naming colors and shapes out loud
  • Coloring with some care inside outlines

On the sheet: Color each shape on the right wing to match the left wing.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 24 · AGES 4 YEARS

Caterpillar Number Writing Worksheet for Age 4

The caterpillar circles are empty — fill them with 1 to 9, in order.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

This cousin of the Counting Caterpillar flips the job: instead of counting printed numbers, your child writes them. Filling a familiar caterpillar shape keeps the order visible — each circle holds exactly one number, and the row itself shows the sequence growing. Counting backwards afterwards (9, 8, 7) is bonus flexibility for little brains.

  • Writing numerals 1 to 9 in order
  • One number per circle discipline
  • Counting backwards from 9
  • Tracing the numeral 9

On the sheet: Write 1 to 9 on the caterpillar, then trace the 9.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 24 · AGES 4 YEARS

Cloud Castle Number Adventure Worksheet for Age 4

Fly the path: write 1 to 10 on the cloud stones, from the bird to the castle.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

A numbered path makes order physical: each stone is one hop, and the numbers grow exactly as the bird gets closer to the castle. Writing on a curved, zigzagging path also builds the flexibility that straight-line worksheets cannot — numbers must land neatly inside clouds that tilt and wander.

  • Writing numerals 1 to 10 in order
  • Following a winding path left to right
  • One number per stone
  • Counting forward and backwards

On the sheet: Write 1 to 10 on the cloud stones along the path.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 24 · AGES 4 YEARS

Counting Balloons Worksheet for Age 4

A party of balloons: count each row, then count them all.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Two neat rows of five balloons make the count honest and checkable: touch each balloon, say the number, write it. The number line underneath gives the count a second life — pointing along 1 to 10 after counting objects is exactly how children move from counting things to knowing the sequence itself.

  • Counting objects one by one to 5
  • Combining 5 and 5 into 10
  • Writing numerals
  • Pointing along a number line

On the sheet: Count the balloons in each row and write the numbers.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 24 · AGES 4 YEARS

Cupcake Bakery Worksheet for Age 4

Count the cupcakes, then share them onto the baker two plates.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Counting comes first — ten cupcakes, five to a row — and then the bakery turns the count into a job: share them onto two plates. Drawing five on each plate is early division with pencils: the same total, two fair groups. Saying five here, five there, ten altogether out loud is the whole lesson in one sentence.

  • Counting objects to 10
  • Sharing a set into two equal groups
  • Drawing a given number of items
  • Saying part-whole sentences

On the sheet: Count the cupcakes, write the total, and draw 5 on each plate.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 24 · AGES 4 YEARS

Dinosaur Egg Rescue Worksheet for Age 4

Number the five eggs in the nest, then draw five more for the rescue.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Five is the friendliest small number: enough to count with one careful finger, small enough to write with growing control. Numbering the nest eggs in order gives 1 to 5 a home, and drawing five more eggs doubles the practice — once as writing numbers, once as producing a set of exactly five.

  • Counting to 5
  • Writing numerals 1 to 5 in order
  • Drawing a given number of objects
  • Decorating with care

On the sheet: Write 1 to 5 on the nest eggs, then draw 5 more eggs below.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 24 · AGES 4 YEARS

Farm Animal Lineup Worksheet for Age 4

Five friends are queueing for the barn: number them first to fifth.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Numbering a line is ordinal thinking — not how many, but which one. The mouse is first, the horse is last, and every animal between has a position to find. Talking through the lineup (who is first? who is between the cat and the horse?) builds the position words children use all day: first, next, last.

  • Ordinal position 1 to 5
  • Writing numerals in line order
  • Using first and last
  • Finding between positions

On the sheet: Write 1 to 5 on the badges, in line order.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 24 · AGES 4 YEARS

Garden Number Path Worksheet for Age 4

Ten stepping stones wind through the garden — number them 1 to 10.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Walking a path with numbers is the oldest counting game there is. Each stone takes exactly one numeral, the curve keeps attention moving forward, and the finish gives a natural stop-and-check: count the stones backwards to see the numbers shrink. Backwards counting sneaks in subtraction rhythm without a single minus sign.

  • Writing numerals 1 to 10 in order
  • Following a curved path
  • Counting forward and backwards
  • One number per stone

On the sheet: Write 1 to 10 on the stepping stones along the garden path.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 24 · AGES 4 YEARS

Giraffe Height Challenge Worksheet for Age 4

Four giraffes, four heights: number them 1 to 4 from shortest to tallest.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Comparing heights means holding a rule in mind and applying it four times — and the artwork trick is that the tallest giraffe is not the first one. Finding the shortest first, then the next, builds systematic comparison instead of pointing at the obvious. The size words at the end (short, shorter, shortest) turn the numbers back into language.

  • Comparing heights
  • Ordering four objects by size
  • Writing numerals 1 to 4
  • Using comparing words

On the sheet: Number the giraffes 1 to 4: 1 is the shortest, 4 is the tallest.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 24 · AGES 4 YEARS

Ice Cream Number Shop Worksheet for Age 4

Count the scoops, then build the cones: 1 scoop, 2 scoops, 3 scoops.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

The shop counts twice: first the whole tub of ten scoops, then little orders of one, two and three. Building cones from the top down — draw one, then two, then three — turns numerals into quantities your child controls. It is counting, drawing and number sense stacked like scoops.

  • Counting objects to 10
  • Drawing 1, 2 and 3 objects
  • Matching numerals to quantities
  • Careful drawing inside a shape

On the sheet: Count the scoops in each row, write the total, and build the three cones.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 24 · AGES 4 YEARS

Little Builder Challenge Worksheet for Age 4

Count the blocks, then build: towers of 3, 4 and 5 on the platforms.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Counting the mixed block row — seven here, five there — is honest counting practice with real shapes: squares, rectangles, triangles, arches. The build task then draws numbers as heights: three blocks stack lower than five, which is how children first feel that 5 is more than 3. Counting the towers afterwards closes the loop.

  • Counting mixed objects to 7
  • Combining 7 and 5 into 12
  • Building sets of 3, 4 and 5
  • Comparing tower heights

On the sheet: Count the blocks in each row, write the total, and build the towers.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 24 · AGES 4 YEARS

Little Pizza Chef Worksheet for Age 4

Top the pizza like a real chef: 5 tomatoes, 5 mushrooms, 5 olives.

Teaching tips
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

A pizza is the happiest counting board in the world. Topping it with exactly five of each ingredient turns draw-5 into a game with a delicious finish, and counting each topping as it lands builds one-to-one discipline: five means five, not six, however hungry the chef. Fifteen toppings all together is a proud big number made of three friendly fives.

  • Drawing a given number of items
  • Counting to 5 three times
  • Keeping count across three groups
  • Saying 5+5+5=15 with fingers

On the sheet: Draw 5 tomato slices, 5 mushrooms and 5 olive rings on the pizza.
